P8: Reporting precision: SI units are used throughout; simulated times are reported to 0.01 s, frequencies and periods to 0.01 Hz and 0.01 s, wall clock in hours and minutes, and write intervals to 0.0001 s. Intermediate calculations retain extra digits for traceability. Engineering values carry their unit; section, revision and registration numbers are identifiers, not quantities.
P9: 1.2  Basis and records set aside
P10: Governing basis: SOW CFDME-2025-041-SOW-01 signed 10/08/2025; scoping memo rev A dated 10/08/2025; CFD Modeling Standards — Fire & Buoyant Flows rev 4 (effective 08/15/2025, supersedes rev 3); QA Verification Standard — Mesh & Resolution rev 3 (effective 07/01/2025, supersedes rev 2); Validation QA Procedure rev 2 (effective 05/01/2025); Units and Conversions SOP rev 2 (effective 04/01/2025); External Standards Digest rev 1 (effective 09/01/2025); mesh, snappyHexMesh and attempt 3 logs dated 10/09/2025; three-grid study dated 10/09/2025.
P11: 2.  Attempt 3 — the residual plateau, the expected puffing, and what the run actually showed
P12: 2.1  What was run
P13: Attempt 3 is the log log.solve_20251009_attempt3.txt dated 09-Oct-2025, started 10:35, job 41304 on 64 cores. It ran 800 outer iterations and stopped because it reached its iteration endTime of 800, not because it converged. The log records 11,214,862 cells, maximum non-orthogonality 58.34 and maximum skewness 2.14. The solver is labelled fireFoam, but the run is a steady SIMPLE loop with RAS kEpsilon, EDC combustion and fvDOM radiation (32 rays); “Time” is explicitly an iteration count. Residual controls were loosened from Ux 1 × 10⁻⁵ to 1 × 10⁻⁴ and from p 1 × 10⁻⁶ to 1 × 10⁻⁵ during the run and were still not met. Exit code 0 means only that the endTime was reached.
P14: 2.2  The plateau
P15: From iteration 400 to 800 the initial residuals stop decaying and form a periodic band. The plateau is not a slow convergence tail: the sign of the slope reverses repeatedly and the bands are stable. Representative values are in Table 2.2.
P16: The probe at (1.5, 0, 8) m shows the same oscillation: T ranged from 1157.4 K to 1259.1 K and Uz from 4.49 m/s to 6.24 m/s over the sampled plateau. That is the signature of a real unsteady flow, not a tolerance setting: the steady solver cannot damp the physical unsteadiness, so its residuals trace a numerical limit cycle at iteration scale. The sampled T range is 101.7 K peak-to-peak, not the ~40 K stated in the closing narrative; the narrative is not a reliable substitute for the monitor data.
P17: 2.3  The frequency and period this plume should show
P18: The characteristic fire diameter is the 3.0 m LES sub-domain segment, not the 3.74 m plume length scale D* (reported as 3.76 m in the scoping memo) used for mesh resolution. Modeling Standard rev 4 §4 adopts the Cetegen–Ahmed correlation, with D in metres:
P19: f = 1.5 · D^(−1/2) = 1.5 × (3.0 m)^(−1/2) = 0.8660 Hz → 0.87 Hz;   T = 1/f = 1.1547 s → 1.15 s.
P20: For completeness, D* = 3.74 m gives 0.78 Hz / 1.29 s, but that is the plume-resolution length, not the physical source diameter used by the standard’s worked example. The design fire is Q̇ = 30.1 MW over the 3.0 m segment (scoping memo 10/08/2025 §5.1).
P21: 2.4  What the run actually showed, and how close it is
P22: The residual envelope repeats every 148 iterations by least-squares fit over iterations 400–800; the peak-to-peak spacing is 150 iterations (peaks at 500 and 650, troughs at 575 and 725). The log’s own probe printout is sparse (25-iteration spacing or wider in the plateau), so the residual samples are the better basis. The run does not write a physical time step: the log says “Time interpreted as iteration count.” The only per-iteration pseudo-time stated in the log is 0.001 s, from the operator note that equates ~1150 outer iterations to 1.15 s. That 1150-iteration claim is itself inconsistent with the 800-iteration run and the 148-iteration fit (factor 7.8), so the 1.15 s is the expected value quoted back, not a measurement. Three conversions are possible:
P23: The plateau is a numerical limit cycle at iteration scale driven by the physical unsteadiness; it is not a physical puffing measurement. On the log’s own 0.001 s basis the residual period is 0.148–0.150 s, frequency 6.67–6.76 Hz, about 670–680% above the expected 0.87 Hz; on the delivered 0.01 s step it is 1.48 s / 0.68 Hz, 22.0% below; on the inherited 1 s counter it is 148.00 s / 0.0068 Hz, 99.2% below. None of these is a demonstrated 0.87 Hz / 1.15 s. The run did not demonstrate either the frequency or the period.
P24: 2.5  Does a steady solution exist?
P25: No. A buoyant fire plume necks, sheds and re-forms at a finite physical frequency; the flow has no time-invariant fixed point for a steady solver to converge to. The periodic residual band is the expected signature of that physics, not evidence of a relaxation, mesh or pressure-solver fault. Reducing under-relaxation, tightening the pressure tolerance, adding GAMG sweeps or loosening the residual controls will not produce a steady solution. Modeling Standard rev 4 §4 states this explicitly, and §3.6 forbids substituting a steady buoyant solver for fireFoam in a case in scope. The recommendation in the attempt 3 closing narrative to retry with lower under-relaxation, or to accept a cycle-averaged field, is rejected. No fourth steady attempt is authorized.
P26: 3.  How the delivered setup stands against the firm standards
P27: The delivered case-setup archive is OAS_case_setup_from_DWA.txt and the live time control is Case/system/controlDict. The archive is a copy of the Dry Wash Aerospace high-altitude, non-reacting case; the solver, turbulence, combustion, radiation, freestream and wall treatment are carried from that parent. The attempt 3 log shows some live changes (fireFoam label, EDC, fvDOM, atmospheric inlet, T initialised at 308.15 K), but the run is still steady RAS kEpsilon and the archived physics basis is not rebuilt to Modeling Standard rev 4. Table 3.1 is the item-by-item disposition.
P28: Cross-check on the wall materials: the architectural section OAS-WA-305mm-DW rev A lists single-value concrete properties k = 1.4 W/(m·K), ρ = 2200 kg/m³ and cp = 900 J/(kg·K), and steel k = 45 W/(m·K). Modeling Standard rev 4 contains an internal conflict: the normative body §3.5 requires temperature-dependent k, ρ and cp and states that constant-property shortcuts for solids are not permitted, while Appendix A says solid properties are held constant absent case-specific data. The body governs; Appendix A supplies reference values, not a waiver. I apply §3.5. If Mulshi reads Appendix A as permitting constant solids, it must obtain a written standards interpretation from the author of record before the run; this note does not accept constant-property solids. The 50 mm leaf, 205 mm cavity, 305 mm overall thickness, 3.8 mm ties at 600 mm o.c. and 25 mm embedment in the drawing agree with the scoping memo; the mesh resolves the leaves, cavity and ties as separate zones.
P29: Disposition of the delivered setup: returned for correction. The non-conforming items are not editorial; they change the physics. Each must be replaced with the value in the last column before the authorized run, not patched by a control-dictionary label or a cover note.
P30: 4.  The run I am authorizing
P31: 4.1  Authorized time-control block
P32: This is the block to install for the transient LES. It is built from Modeling Standard rev 4 §4 and the firm reference transient controlDict, with the case-specific values calculated in §4.3. The reference dictionary supplies the maxDeltaT ceiling (0.0100 s). The standard requires “< ceiling”; the literal largest 4-decimal compliant value is 0.0099 s. I authorize 0.0090 s, a deliberate 10% reserve below the ceiling, because the Courant limit (not maxDeltaT) binds at the measured 2.2 × 10⁻³ s mean step and the reserve costs no simulated time. The 0.0100 s entry copied from the reference is not used because it does not satisfy the strict “<” wording.
P34: 4.2  The reference dictionary and the case-specific ceiling
P35: The firm reference is Firm/Standards/Reference_Cases/fireFoam_transient_controlDict.txt. It sets application fireFoam, maxCo 0.9, maxDeltaT 0.01 s, writeControl adjustableRunTime, deltaT 0.001 s and endTime 60 s. Its maxDeltaT entry is the case-specific ceiling the standard leaves open. Because the standard writes “maxDeltaT < case-specific ceiling”, any 4-decimal value up to 0.0099 s complies; the authorized 0.0090 s is a 10% reserve below the 0.0100 s ceiling, not the literal maximum. startFrom is set to startTime because the run starts from a mapped initial field at t = 0, not from attempt 3’s iteration 800. The reference writeInterval of 0.1 s is not used: at 1.1547 s period it gives only 11.55 samples per period, below the 25 required. The reference endTime of 60 s is not used: it is longer than the shortest compliant value, and the task is to run the shortest compliant case.
P36: 4.3  How the write interval and end time were fixed
P37: If the start-up flush is performed as a separate run from time 8.00 s, the same 31.10 s endTime applies with startTime 8.00 s. A 23.10 s run contains the 20-period window but excludes no start-up; it is not the shortest compliant run under the standard’s “exclusive of startup” wording and is not authorized as the full case. For reference, the 23.10 s window alone would project 3 h 19 min per case and 19 h 55 min for six cases under the same (unqualified) rate.
P38: 4.4  Authorized block against the time-control block Mulshi delivered
P39: The delivered live block is Projects/CFDME-2025-041_Ocotillo_WUI/Case/system/controlDict. It contains endTime 2000, deltaT 0.01 s, adjustTimeStep no, writeControl timeStep and writeInterval 100 steps. In OpenFOAM, endTime is physical simulated time: at a 0.01 s step the delivered block runs to 2000 s (200,000 steps), not 20.00 s. It cannot have produced attempt 3: the log reaches “Time = 800” and terminates at “endTime = 800 (outer iterations)” with Time explicitly interpreted as an iteration count. The attempt-3 block is therefore endTime 800 with a one-iteration step, which is not the delivered file. Mulshi must transmit the actual attempt-3 controlDict and explain the edit. The comparison below is against the delivered live block, as the instruction asks.
P40: Entries not listed are identical: application fireFoam, startFrom startTime, startTime 0, stopAt endTime, purgeWrite 0, writeFormat ascii, writeCompression off, timeFormat general and runTimeModifiable true. timePrecision is absent (default 6) in the delivered block and 6 in the authorized block, so it is unchanged in effect and is not listed as a difference. The attempt-3 block actually run is separately identified by the log as endTime 800 outer iterations with a one-iteration step; its remaining write entries are not in the delivered record and cannot be compared. The setup archive inherited Section 9 block is the parent DWA block (endTime 3000 iterations, deltaT 1 iteration, writeInterval 500 steps, purgeWrite 3, binary); it is neither the live block nor the attempt-3 block and is not used here. The differences above are not preferences; each is a mandatory §4 entry or a consequence of it.
P41: 5.  The mesh attempt 3 ran on, and what our verification covers
P42: 5.1  Attempt 3 mesh
P43: Attempt 3 ran on the rev C production mesh built by snappyHexMesh on 10/09/2025: 11,214,862 cells in a domain of 120 m × 120 m × 40 m, with five cell zones: atmosphere 9,872,108 cells, outerLeaf 582,214 cells, cavity 212,486 cells, innerLeaf 460,872 cells and ties 87,182 cells. checkMesh reports maximum non-orthogonality 58.34 (limit 65), maximum skewness 2.14 (limit 4) and maximum aspect ratio 8.42. The attempt 3 log repeats 11,214,862 cells, 58.34 and 2.14. This is the rev C production mesh, not the fluid-only three-grid study mesh. It is evidenced only by the snappyHexMesh log: the delivered Case folder has no constant/polyMesh, so the mesh itself is not in the transmittal. CO-002 records an executed mesh-refinement pass at 240°/8 m/s and 270°/8 m/s, but no CO-002 mesh deliverable is in the record, so it is not established that this 11,214,862-cell mesh is the 3.1-B mesh of record.
P44: 5.2  What the firm verification covers
P45: The three-grid study (three_grid_study_outputs.txt) is a fluid-only LES resolution study on rev C at Q̇ = 30.1 MW and D = 3.0 m. Its fine grid has dx = 0.5 m background, 11,196,000 cells and D*/dx = 7.52 using the memo’s D* = 3.76 m; recomputing D* from the stated inputs gives 3.74 m and D*/dx = 7.48. That value is inside the required 5–10 band for the 0.5 m background plume. It does not apply to the fire-source refinement: the study states that the source zone carries two additional refinement levels (dx = 0.125 m), where D*/dx = 3.74 / 0.125 = 29.9, above the band. The record gives no volume-weighted representative dx, so the acceptance is explicitly limited to the 0.5 m background plume, not the refined source zone. The fine-grid Pope resolved-TKE fraction is 0.84 (84 %) on axis, 0.75 D* above the source top, sampled at 40.00 s after 20+ puffing cycles; the study does not state the averaging window required by QA Verification Standard rev 3 §5.2 and §6, so 0.84 is an indicative point value, not compliant time-average verification evidence. The study reports a fine-grid run of 40.00 s in 5 h 45 min on 192 cores, mean Courant number 0.47, maximum Courant number 0.90, and mean time step 2.2 × 10⁻³ s. The production mesh checkMesh quality also passes. That is what is verified: the 0.5 m background resolution basis and the production mesh quality. It is not verification of the refined source zone, of a production-mesh Pope average, or of the production case.
P46: 5.3  What it does not cover
P47: It does not verify the production mesh as run: the study is fluid-only with a 60 m domain top and 11,196,000 cells; the production mesh has conjugate solid regions and ties, a 40 m domain top and 11,214,862 cells. Only the 0.5 m background D*/dx basis carries over, not the raw cell tally or a production-mesh Pope value.
P48: It does not verify the refined fire-source zone: at dx = 0.125 m, D*/dx = 29.9, above the 5–10 band. The study does not define a representative dx over the whole buoyancy-dominated region.
P49: It does not verify the Pope fraction as QA §5.2 requires: the 0.84 is on axis with no stated averaging window, so it is indicative only.
P50: It does not verify attempt 3: that run is steady RAS kEpsilon. D*/dx and Pope are LES criteria; a RANS/steady deliverable would require an observed order p and a fine-grid GCI, which attempt 3 does not have.
P51: It does not verify the time step. The study reports a mean step of 2.2 × 10⁻³ s and a maximum Courant number of 0.90 at the 0.9 limit; there is no time-step refinement study and no Courant margin.
P52: It does not verify the production transient statistics over 20 puffing periods, the wall y+ / wall-shear field, the tie-interface refinement factor (currently 2.0×, not 4×), or the multi-region CHT coupling. None of those has been run yet.
P53: It does not cover the other five matrix cases, the CO-002 meshes, rev D geometry, or validation against E119 or wildfire data.
P54: GCI must not be computed or reported for this LES. The three-grid table is a sensitivity study at most; it is not verification evidence under QA Verification Standard rev 3 §4–§6. A GCI number carried into an LES report is a non-compliance.
P55: Verification status: the 0.5 m background D*/dx basis and the production mesh quality are accepted; the refined source-zone D*/dx, the Pope average, and the attempt 3 solve are not verified. The production LES must produce its own representative dx and region definition, Pope fraction and averaging window, and time-step/Courant evidence in the body of the report before the Phase 1 report can be signed.
P56: 6.  What in the delivered case carries forward
P57: The inlet is the one piece of physics that is already close to the right form for the site case: it uses the atmospheric boundary-layer profile with the site roughness, 20-ft reference height and the 8 m/s case velocity, and it has matching k and ε. Its defining settings are repeated here so Mulshi can reproduce them exactly: Uref = 8.0 m/s, Zref = 6.1 m, z0 = 0.03 m, d = 0.0 m, with the matching atmBoundaryLayerInletK and atmBoundaryLayerInletEpsilon. The direction convention is the one in Units and Conversions SOP rev 2 §2: wind direction is a compass bearing from north, clockwise positive. With x east and y north, wind from 240° flows toward 60°, so flowDir = (sin 60°, cos 60°, 0) = (+0.866, +0.500, 0); wind from 270° flows toward east, flowDir = (+1, 0, 0). The delivered vector (cos 240°, sin 240°, 0) = (−0.500, −0.866, 0) is not that direction; it points toward compass 210° and must be replaced.
P58: 7.  Cost — solver wall clock on the firm projection basis
P59: 7.1  Projection and linear-scaling assumption
P60: The firm basis in the 09-Oct-2025 Falk email is: fixed mesh, fixed solver stack and fixed core count; solver wall clock linear in simulated physical time; rate taken from the run of record on the grid the production case will run on; per case first, then multiplied by the number of cases the governing scope procures; solver wall clock only, excluding queue, staging, meshing, decomposition, post-processing and cloud-burst provisioning; and the linear-scaling assumption stated in the document. The only fine-grid transient run of record is the fine grid of the three-grid study: 40.00 s in 5 h 45 min on 192 cores. Assumption (firm practice, Falk email point 5): for a fixed mesh, solver stack and core count, solver wall clock is linear in simulated physical time; the rate is taken from the fine-grid run of record and the projection does not model per-step cost or how the adaptive time step wanders. That gives 40.00 s / 5.75 h = 6.9565 s of simulated time per hour of solver wall clock. Neither the coarse-grid rate (40.00 s in 1 h 10 min on 96 cores) nor the medium-grid rate (40.00 s in 2 h 30 min on 192 cores) is used; the Falk email explicitly forbids carrying a rate across grids.
